review_material.assessment: The source provides a quantitative, exactly solvable transition for the Toric code under bit-flip (Pauli-X) incoherent errors, with a critical error rate p_c^(2)=0.178 and a mapping to the 2D classical Ising universality class. The open string operator W_{m\bar{m}} is defined and its behavior in the topological and condensed phases is described. The TEE is computed as 2 log 2 below and log 2 above the transition. This supports a quantitative cluster with one control (error rate p), one readout (open string expectation value), and a mechanism with the critical parameter. The source also provides the relation mu = tanh^{-1}[p/(1-p)] and the critical mu_c = (1/4) log(1+sqrt(2)). The extraction is limited to this single best cluster; other examples (double semion, Laughlin) are qualitative and not selected. The case is authoring-ready because there is a numeric control, a numeric readout, a quantitative mechanism, and an objective source-grounded response within an explicit domain.

claims.applicability: The claim applies to the Toric code on a square lattice subject to local bit-flip (Pauli-X) incoherent errors, in the errorfield double (second moment) formulation. The transition is exactly solvable and of 2D classical Ising universality. The open string operator is defined for an open path \calP on the lattice.

anchors.support: The Toric code subject to bit-flip errors: the Kraus operator creates two m anyons, the EFD is given by exp(mu sum (m\bar{m})_r (m\bar{m})_{r'}) with mu = tanh^{-1}[p/(1-p)], and anyon condensation of m\bar{m} occurs at p_c^{(2)} = 0.178 in the 2D classical Ising universality class.

The EFD for Toric code with bit-flip errors is written as \kket{\rho} = \prod_l ((1-p)+p X_l\otimes X_l) \ket{\Psi_0}\otimes\ket{\Psi_0^*} \propto e^{\mu \sum_i X_l\otimes X_l} \ket{\Psi_0}\otimes\ket{\Psi_0^*}, with mu = tanh^{-1}[p/(1-p)].

The loop model reduces to the square lattice Ising model with H = sum -2 mu sigma_i sigma_j, the transition is of 2D classical Ising universality, and the critical point is mu_c = (1/4) log(1+sqrt(2)), i.e. p_c^{(2)} = 0.178.
The critical point is exactly solvable and determined by the Kramers-Wannier duality, mu_c = (1/4) log(1+sqrt(2)), i.e. p_c^(2) = 0.178.

mechanisms.statement: Bit-flip (Pauli-X) errors on the Toric code create paired m\bar{m} anyons in the errorfield double, which condense at a critical error rate p_c^(2)=0.178, driving a transition in the 2D classical Ising universality class.

review_material.paper_scope: The paper develops an effective field theory for decoherence-induced transitions in Abelian topologically ordered states, focusing on the errorfield double (EFD) formulation. It analyzes the Toric code under bit-flip errors, deriving an exactly solvable anyon condensation transition at p_c^(2)=0.178, and classifies phases for Toric code, double semion, and Laughlin states. The selected quantitative cluster is the Toric code bit-flip transition and its open string order parameter.

anchors.support: The anyon condensation can be detected by the open string operator \langle\!\langle W_{m\overline{m}}(\calP)\rangle\!\rangle := \frac{\bbra{\rho} W_{m\overline{m}}(\calP) \kket{\rho}}{\bbrakket{\rho}{\rho}} = \frac{\tr\rho\, w_m(\calP)\, \rho\, w_m^\dagger(\calP)}{\tr \rho^2}, where w_m(\calP) := \prod_{i\in\calP} X_i.

The anyon condensation transition is detected by the open string operator \langle\!\langle W_{m\overline{m}}(\calP)\rangle\!\rangle = \frac{\bbra{\rho} w_m(\calP)\otimes w_{\overline{m}}(\calP) \kket{\rho}}{\bbrakket{\rho}{\rho}} = \frac{1}{\calZ(\mu)}\sum_{g,h} (-1)^{\#\text{crossing}(\calP,h)} e^{-4\mu|h|}, where \#\text{crossing}(\calP,h) counts crossings between the open string and loop h.

source_ambiguities.statement: The open string operator is defined in the main text as \langle\!\langle W_{m\overline{m}}(\calP)\rangle\!\rangle = \frac{\tr\rho\, w_m(\calP)\, \rho\, w_m^\dagger(\calP)}{\tr \rho^2}, while in the supplementary material it is written as \frac{\bbra{\rho} w_m(\calP)\otimes w_{\overline{m}}(\calP) \kket{\rho}}{\bbrakket{\rho}{\rho}} = \frac{1}{\calZ(\mu)}\sum_{g,h} (-1)^{\#\text{crossing}(\calP,h)} e^{-4\mu|h|}.
